prerequisites: Basic command of fundamental theorems and trigonometric relations, complex numbers, systems of linear equations, and differential and integral calculus of single-variable functions.
Knowledge of the physical fundamentals of Electrical Engineering.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and use of the principles of circuit theory and electrical machines.
Knowledge of basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.

Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering, ELECTRICAL SPECIFIC TECHNOLOGY.
Adopt a responsible, orderly attitude at work and be willing to learn, considering the challenge that continuous training will pose.

Apply the strategies of the scientific methodology: analyze the problematic situation qualitatively and quantitatively, propose hypotheses and solutions using the models typical of industrial engineering, Electrical specialty.
Work effectively in a group, integrating capacities and knowledge to make decisions in the field of industrial engineering, Electrical specialty.
Know and be able to precisely describe the behavior of basic elements in direct current and sinusoidal periodic alternating current circuits.
Know the basic principles of electrical circuit theory and its application to the precise calculation of direct current and alternating current electrical circuits.
Understand the importance of three-phase systems and acquire sufficient knowledge for the analysis and calculation of balanced voltage systems.

Know, understand, analyze, and distinguish the constitution, operation, and application of different types of electrical machines, as well as select the most suitable type of electrical machine for the various needs that may arise in the industrial environment.
Consistently use the course knowledge to solve circuit and electrical machine problems.
Apply theoretical knowledge to carry out laboratory setups and tests. Understand and interpret the results, clearly and rigorously drafting the corresponding reports.
Work in a team to undertake cooperative tasks. Make proposals, analyze contributions from others, discuss ideas, search for information from various sources, and execute the corresponding actions.
Communicate correctly orally and in writing, using appropriate technological resources, the concepts and principles of circuits and electrical machines.
Adopt a positive attitude towards learning about circuits and electrical machines, being participative and demonstrating a spirit of overcoming learning difficulties.

syllabus_topics: Variables and elements of electrical circuits: Introduction, Variables of electrical circuits (definition, units, and relationships), Elements of electrical circuits (definition, physical interpretation, operational impedance and admittance, element association), Basic circuit laws.

Waveforms: Constant and periodic waveforms, Behavior of basic elements in direct current and sinusoidal periodic alternating current circuits, Powers (physical interpretation), Measurement of electrical parameters and magnitudes, Application examples.
Circuit analysis methods: Network topology, Source transformation, Circuit analysis by circular equations (meshes and loops), Circuit analysis by nodal equations (nodes), Application examples.
Network theorems: Introduction, Linearity, Superposition, Thévenin, Norton, Millman, and maximum power transfer theorems.

Balanced three-phase voltage systems: Introduction, Balanced voltage systems (phase sequence, simple and compound voltage, star and delta loads), Calculation of three-phase systems, Power measurement.

Magnetic circuits and transformers: Basic concepts of magnetic circuits, Magnetic materials, Laws of magnetic circuits, Losses in ferromagnetic cores, Transformers (Introduction, constructive aspects, operating principle, functional characteristics, basic calculations, and applications).
Rotating electrical machines: asynchronous and synchronous: Introduction, constructive aspects, operating principles, functional characteristics, applications, and selection of machine type.
teaching_methods: Lectures (magistral sessions) where the teacher explains content and solves application exercises.
In-class tasks, individually or in groups, related to explained content, to be submitted at the end of the session.
Laboratory practices where the teacher explains the exercises, and students work in groups to perform them.
Group reports on laboratory practices, to be submitted after each session.
Prior reading of documentation provided via the eGela platform is recommended for students to clarify doubts during class.
assessment_rules: For continuous evaluation, a global grade equal to or greater than 5 is required to pass. The theory and exercise exam (50%) has four blocks, each requiring a minimum score of 4/10; a weighted average of 5 or more is also needed for this component. The laboratory exam (15%) requires a minimum score of 5/10 for each part. Laboratory reports (20%) and in-class tasks (15%) do not require a minimum score. If the minimum score is not met in any component, the maximum grade recorded will be 4.5. Students can opt out of continuous evaluation within specific deadlines, in which case a final exam covers 100% of the material, requiring approval in each of its parts (Written theory and problems: 50%, Oral and/or written lab practical exam: 15%, Exercise solving: 15%, Lab practical work/questionnaire: 20%). Grades from partial tests are saved for the current academic year if the minimum qualification is surpassed; no grades are saved for future calls in the final evaluation method.
